I won't give you the letter for q3, even in a practice retake. A quiz item stays closed until it's graded, and I don't confirm or rule out options either. Neither of your attempts has been graded yet, so the item is still closed. Reading up on why later would also mean you never get to practice working the answer out.

Here's a way to work it out yourself. It applies to every option equally.

Start with what's going wrong in the scenario. After 40 steps, the agent repeats the same edit and gets the same failing test, and the whole history is still in its context. So the question is whether the agent is failing for lack of something, or whether the loop itself has no way to notice that it's stuck.

Then take each option and ask two things:
1. Does this change the **agent program** (the code around the model), or only what the model is given or how big its input can be?
2. If the model keeps behaving the way it did for 40 steps, would this change make the loop behave differently on step 41?

You can also bring in the loop from your learning record. The model asks for an action, the program runs it, the result comes back, and it repeats. Ask which part of that cycle decides when the cycle ends.

This also ties to your budget. Each extra model call costs money, so think about what a repeating loop does to your cost per request.

Tell me which option you'd pick and why, in your own words. Once quiz 0001 is graded, I'll go through q3 with you in full, along with your other answers. I can grade your two submissions now if you want that.
